info.name: FinTrack API
info.description:
# FinTrack API

Personal finance tracker: users own accounts, accounts hold transactions,
categories classify them.

## How to run this collection

1. Import `docs/fintrack.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Set `base_url` to your local or deployed URL.
3. Run **01 Auth > Login (user)** and **01 Auth > Login (admin)** first - their
   test scripts write `access_token` and `admin_token` into the environment,
   and every other request reads them from there.
4. Everything else can then be run in order, or with the Collection Runner.

All seeded users share the password `Password123!`.

## Folder 06

Folder **06 Security** contains the deliberately blocked requests: no token,
a foreign account id, a non-admin write, and the login rate limit.

item.description: Shared reference data. Any user can read; only an admin can write (RBAC).

item.name: 05 Transactions
item.description: Full CRUD. Every write recalculates the owning account balance inside one database transaction.

request.description: Check GET /accounts/3 afterwards: the balance drops by exactly 46 500.
A transfer carries no category. The canonical schema has no destination column, so a transfer does not move this account balance - see "Known limitations" in the README.

item.name: POST /transactions (400 - three broken rules at once)

request.description: VALIDATION ERROR: bad enum, non-positive amount, and a date that matches the format but does not exist.

item.name: POST /transactions (400 - income category on an expense)

request.description: Domain rule beyond what a CHECK constraint can express: the category type has to agree with the transaction type.

exec: pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('cannot be used on a expense transaction');

request.description: Only transactions on accounts the caller owns.
Query parameters go through the same ValidationPipe as request bodies.
Raising an expense from 46 500 to 52 000 takes another 5 500 off the account - the service applies the difference, not the new amount.
An explicit null clears the category. Omitting the field would keep the old one and be rejected, because a transfer must not carry a category.
